bull_bear.body:
- Long operating history — incorporated in 1986, presenting its 42nd Annual Report for FY 2025-26, having transformed from a family-led enterprise into a professionally managed, publicly listed organisation
- Overseas manufacturing footprint through a 100%-owned Vietnam subsidiary (Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd.), giving the group a presence outside India
- Stated absence of leverage-related distress markers: no public deposits outstanding as at 31 March 2026, no funds raised through debt securities during the year, and no proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
- All properties including buildings, plant and machinery and inventories were stated to be adequately insured during FY 2025-26
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff exposure on the export/overseas business — The Directors' Report attributes the decline in consolidated profitability primarily to the impact of tariff measures imposed by the United States of America. This is the only cause management names for the consolidated shortfall, making trade-policy action on the group's export markets a structural, recurring exposure rather than a one-off.
- Geopolitical uncertainty and war-like situations disrupting global trade — Management explicitly cites 'prevailing geopolitical uncertainties, including war-like situations in various regions, which adversely affected global trade and business conditions' as a driver of the consolidated profit decline — an exogenous demand and logistics risk it cannot mitigate internally.
- Dependence of standalone profitability on other income rather than operations — The Directors' Report states that standalone revenue from operations decreased while other income rose substantially, and that the group-level result diverged sharply from the standalone result. Earnings quality therefore rests partly on non-operating income. (No figures reproduced here — the underlying table is a primary financial statement.)
- Concentration of the group's operations in a single overseas subsidiary — The consolidated result is materially different from the standalone result, indicating the overseas subsidiary carries a significant share of group activity; a shock to that single geography flows straight through to consolidated earnings.
- No Risk Management Committee constituted — Because the Company was not among the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as on 31st March 2026, constituting a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of SEBI LODR was not mandatory and none was constituted. Risk oversight rests on the full Board's periodic review rather than a dedicated committee.
- No credit rating obtained — The Company states it did not obtain any credit rating during FY 2025-26, so there is no third-party assessment of its credit quality for lenders or investors to reference.
- Reliance on a Board-level risk framework with no disclosed risk register — The AR describes an 'adequate and effective Risk Management Framework' in generic terms — identification, evaluation, mitigation and monitoring reviewed periodically by the Board — but the routed text contains no MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' section enumerating the specific risks or their mitigations, so the framework cannot be assessed against named exposures.

- Long operating history — incorporated in 1986, presenting its 42nd Annual Report for FY 2025-26, having transformed from a family-led enterprise into a professionally managed, publicly listed organisation
- Overseas manufacturing footprint through a 100%-owned Vietnam subsidiary (Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd.), giving the group a presence outside India
- Stated absence of leverage-related distress markers: no public deposits outstanding as at 31 March 2026, no funds raised through debt securities during the year, and no proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
- All properties including buildings, plant and machinery and inventories were stated to be adequately insured during FY 2025-26
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Stay with the core business of manufacturing woven and knitted elastic tapes — there was no change in the nature of business during FY 2025-26.
- Pursue growth through product diversification, process improvements and expansion of the customer base.
- Leverage industry expertise, technological capabilities and market presence to enhance stakeholder value.
- Keep the group structure unchanged, operating overseas through the existing wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited; no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year.
- Management continues to assess strategic options for the Vietnam subsidiary (PGVCL), with the Board having considered the need for an impairment assessment.
- The routed governance sections state no formal dividend policy or payout framework. For FY 2025-26 the 42nd AGM is asked to confirm the payment of interim dividends (including a special dividend) on equity shares and to declare a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share of face value Rs 10. The Company has not issued any convertible instruments and, as on March 31, 2026, the Non-Executive Independent Directors hold no equity shares in the Company.
- BRSR is not applicable: as the Company did not fall within the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as at 31st March 2026, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report was not required for FY 2025-26 and none is furnished — a stated absence, so no BRSR-based ESG metrics or targets exist for this year.
- PoSH: zero tolerance policy adopted covering all employees including trainees, apprentices and probationers at all locations, with awareness and sensitisation programmes; the Directors state there were no cases filed or pending during the year under review.
- Maternity benefits: the Company confirms compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 — all eligible women employees received paid maternity leave, continuity of service and salary, plus post-maternity support such as nursing breaks and flexible work arrangements where applicable.
- Whistle-blower policy with a vigil mechanism extended to Directors, employees and value chain partners, covering unethical conduct, actual or suspected fraud, Code of Conduct violations and leaks of UPSI, with protection against retaliation.
- Code of Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading plus a Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of UPSI, governing trading by Designated Persons and their immediate relatives.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no named capex or expansion project, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no plant/capacity addition. The only forward capital-deployment statement is a reinvestment intent: the Board proposed no transfer to the General Reserve and the entire earnings for FY 2025-26, after payment of dividend, are to be retained in the Profit & Loss Account 'to support future business expansion, technological upgradation, and strategic initiatives'. There was no change in the nature of business during the year and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate; the Company continues to operate overseas through its existing wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited. Share capital was unchanged during the year, no shares or convertible securities were issued, and no options were granted, vested, exercised or lapsed under the ESOP Scheme 2017. Against this, the named capital-commitments disclosure states that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for was NIL as at 31st March 2026 — i.e. the Company had no contracted capex pipeline at the balance-sheet date.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company's core business is the manufacture of woven and knitted elastic tapes; its stated vision is to become a leading manufacturer of woven and knitted elastic tapes. It operates in India and, through its wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited, in Vietnam. The annual report under review is the Company's 42nd, for the financial year ended 31st March 2026.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding, incorporated in Vietnam; reporting period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, different from the holding company's reporting period; reporting currency VND. Per Form AOC-1, Part A: Subsidiaries. Financials of the subsidiary deliberately not reproduced.
- Premco Industries — associate: Listed under 'Associates' in the related-party note as an enterprise on which significant influence is exercised, having common directors/partners. Note: the Directors' Report separately states the Company has no Joint Venture / Associate Companies under the Companies Act definition, so this is a related-party 'associate enterprise' rather than an Act-defined associate company.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Export markets — the Company incurs export-related expenses and its consolidated performance was stated to be affected by tariff measures imposed by the United States of America
- Vietnam — operations conducted through the wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Stay with the core business of manufacturing woven and knitted elastic tapes — there was no change in the nature of business during FY 2025-26.
- Pursue growth through product diversification, process improvements and expansion of the customer base.
- Leverage industry expertise, technological capabilities and market presence to enhance stakeholder value.
- Keep the group structure unchanged, operating overseas through the existing wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited; no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year.
- Management continues to assess strategic options for the Vietnam subsidiary (PGVCL), with the Board having considered the need for an impairment assessment.
- The routed governance sections state no formal dividend policy or payout framework. For FY 2025-26 the 42nd AGM is asked to confirm the payment of interim dividends (including a special dividend) on equity shares and to declare a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share of face value Rs 10. The Company has not issued any convertible instruments and, as on March 31, 2026, the Non-Executive Independent Directors hold no equity shares in the Company.
- BRSR is not applicable: as the Company did not fall within the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as at 31st March 2026, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report was not required for FY 2025-26 and none is furnished — a stated absence, so no BRSR-based ESG metrics or targets exist for this year.
- PoSH: zero tolerance policy adopted covering all employees including trainees, apprentices and probationers at all locations, with awareness and sensitisation programmes; the Directors state there were no cases filed or pending during the year under review.
- Maternity benefits: the Company confirms compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 — all eligible women employees received paid maternity leave, continuity of service and salary, plus post-maternity support such as nursing breaks and flexible work arrangements where applicable.
- Whistle-blower policy with a vigil mechanism extended to Directors, employees and value chain partners, covering unethical conduct, actual or suspected fraud, Code of Conduct violations and leaks of UPSI, with protection against retaliation.
- Code of Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading plus a Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of UPSI, governing trading by Designated Persons and their immediate relatives.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no named capex or expansion project, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no plant/capacity addition. The only forward capital-deployment statement is a reinvestment intent: the Board proposed no transfer to the General Reserve and the entire earnings for FY 2025-26, after payment of dividend, are to be retained in the Profit & Loss Account 'to support future business expansion, technological upgradation, and strategic initiatives'. There was no change in the nature of business during the year and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate; the Company continues to operate overseas through its existing wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited. Share capital was unchanged during the year, no shares or convertible securities were issued, and no options were granted, vested, exercised or lapsed under the ESOP Scheme 2017. Against this, the named capital-commitments disclosure states that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for was NIL as at 31st March 2026 — i.e. the Company had no contracted capex pipeline at the balance-sheet date.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long operating history — incorporated in 1986, presenting its 42nd Annual Report for FY 2025-26, having transformed from a family-led enterprise into a professionally managed, publicly listed organisation
- Overseas manufacturing footprint through a 100%-owned Vietnam subsidiary (Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd.), giving the group a presence outside India
- Stated absence of leverage-related distress markers: no public deposits outstanding as at 31 March 2026, no funds raised through debt securities during the year, and no proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
- All properties including buildings, plant and machinery and inventories were stated to be adequately insured during FY 2025-26

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- US tariff exposure on the export/overseas business — The Directors' Report attributes the decline in consolidated profitability primarily to the impact of tariff measures imposed by the United States of America. This is the only cause management names for the consolidated shortfall, making trade-policy action on the group's export markets a structural, recurring exposure rather than a one-off.
- Geopolitical uncertainty and war-like situations disrupting global trade — Management explicitly cites 'prevailing geopolitical uncertainties, including war-like situations in various regions, which adversely affected global trade and business conditions' as a driver of the consolidated profit decline — an exogenous demand and logistics risk it cannot mitigate internally.
- Dependence of standalone profitability on other income rather than operations — The Directors' Report states that standalone revenue from operations decreased while other income rose substantially, and that the group-level result diverged sharply from the standalone result. Earnings quality therefore rests partly on non-operating income. (No figures reproduced here — the underlying table is a primary financial statement.)
- Concentration of the group's operations in a single overseas subsidiary — The consolidated result is materially different from the standalone result, indicating the overseas subsidiary carries a significant share of group activity; a shock to that single geography flows straight through to consolidated earnings.
- No Risk Management Committee constituted — Because the Company was not among the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as on 31st March 2026, constituting a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of SEBI LODR was not mandatory and none was constituted. Risk oversight rests on the full Board's periodic review rather than a dedicated committee.
- No credit rating obtained — The Company states it did not obtain any credit rating during FY 2025-26, so there is no third-party assessment of its credit quality for lenders or investors to reference.
- Reliance on a Board-level risk framework with no disclosed risk register — The AR describes an 'adequate and effective Risk Management Framework' in generic terms — identification, evaluation, mitigation and monitoring reviewed periodically by the Board — but the routed text contains no MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' section enumerating the specific risks or their mitigations, so the framework cannot be assessed against named exposures.
